To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BvgA is a transcriptional activator for virulence-associated genes of Bordetella pertusis and that it interacts specifically with the α subunit of B. pertusis RNA polymerase.

the E. coli RNA polymerase α subunit is absolutely required to activate the lac promoter and that B. pertussic virulence-associated genes, in the presenceof their activator, can be transcribed by all of the hybrids tested.

the B. pertussi s RNA polymerase subunit α, which is essential for transcription of B. pertus s virulence-associated genes in the presence of BvgA, is not essential for the transcription of E. coli genes in the presence or absence of cyclic AMP and catabolite gene-activator protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of transcriptional regulation of the pertussis toxin gene, a virulence determinant of B. pertusis.
the molecular mechanism of transcriptional regulation in the bacterial pathogen B. pertussus.
the mechanism of transcriptional activation of B. pertusis virulence-associated genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hybrid polymerase system is a useful tool in studying the molecular basis for promoter selectivity.
the hybrid RNA polymerases are able to recognize the promoters of both B. pertussi and E. coli and to initiate transcription, but with a different efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the α subunit of E. coli RNA polymerase is a key element of the activator recognition site, whereas the β subunit is not.
B. pertussic and E. coli promoters can be activated by hybrid RNA polymerases containing the E. coli β subunit and the B. pertussi α subunit.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the α subunit, in the context of the hybrid polymerases, is not a general transcriptional regulator, and it may be that the α subunits of RNA polymerases are not involved in transcriptional regulation in general.
the B. pertussishybrid α subunit is not a simple E. coli α homologue but has a distinct structure.
